facts.fact: The health ministry's E-Health Strategy 2012-2017 names the District Health Information System (DHIS) as the national HMIS and lists its strengthening among the e-health applications under way; the document is undated, so the year is its published date.

The health ministry's E-Health Strategy 2012-2017 states that the DHIS is deployed throughout the country and captures data from all 67 districts, with mobile phones being added for remote facilities reporting to the national database; it does not say in so many words where the data is keyed, and the year is the undated document's published date.

The health ministry's E-Health Strategy 2012-2017 says mobile phones are being used in remote facilities to report to the national DHIS database but gives no number or share of facilities doing so; the year is the undated document's published date.

systems.tiers: all 67 districts; remote facilities by mobile phone

systems.owner: Ministry of Health and Child Welfare with the regulatory authorities

note: No EMR fact: the strategy treats electronic medical records and a shared patient record as priorities and architecture to be built, and names no deployed EMR. The digitised:district value rests on the 'all 67 districts' wording, not on an explicit statement of where data is keyed.
